finding: I cannot write the test "a filtered mutation probe at a fresh head obtains a baseline". §5.2.4 defines the new field as "`probe` when the run was performed as part of a probe", and §5.2.6 now adds "Only a run record carrying no `probe` may serve as a baseline." But §5.2.2 mandates a run that exists only because a probe was requested: "A filtered mutation probe MUST additionally record a filtered baseline for the same filter on unmutated code", and §5.2.6 itself requires that "when no matching run exists at the current head, [`cr probe run`] MUST perform and record it before the probe". Implementation A stamps `probe` on that run — it was literally performed as part of a probe run — and §5.2.6 then disqualifies it, so `baseline` (required in §5.5) can never be filled and every filtered mutation probe at a fresh head aborts. Implementation B reads "as part of a probe" as "executed the probe's mutated code", leaves the baseline unstamped, and the probe runs. §5.5's "unmutated, un-probed code" does not settle it: that phrase describes the code state measured, not which invocation recorded the run.
suggestion: Pin the field in §5.2.4 to the mutated execution: "`probe` when the run executed the probe's mutated code or its supplied test file; a baseline recorded per §5.2.2 or §5.2.6 carries none."

finding: The round-10 repair to §5.2 deadlocks the first probe at every head. §5.2.4 requires a run record to carry "`probe` when the run was performed as part of a probe", and §5.2.6's new final sentence says "Only a run record carrying no `probe` may serve as a baseline." But the same item §5.2.6 makes `cr probe run` the producer of the missing baseline: "when no matching run exists at the current head, MUST perform and record it before the probe." That baseline run is performed as part of a probe on §5.2.4's literal wording, so `cr` stamps `probe` on it and the very next sentence disqualifies it. §5.5 marks `baseline` required, and §5.3.5 and §5.4.4 both condition support on the baseline's `passed`, so no mutation or gap probe can ever be recorded at a fresh head. Nothing in §5.2.4 distinguishes the probe's measured run (which must be excluded) from the baseline run performed alongside it (which must be admitted); §5.5's `baseline` row carries the real intent — "measuring the same tests on unmutated, un-probed code" — but §5.2.4's condition is about who ran it, not what it measured.
suggestion: Narrow §5.2.4's condition to the measured run: replace "`probe` when the run was performed as part of a probe" with "`probe` when the run measured mutated or probe-added code".

finding: The only path from a gap probe to a `probed` grade runs entirely on inputs `cr` cannot evaluate. §5.4.4: "The probe MUST be treated as supporting the finding only when its baseline passed per §5.2.5 **and** the finding's `claim` field names the claim the test asserts" — the second conjunct is not machine-checkable. `cr` never reads the test file's semantics, so it can establish only that `claim` is set; whether the supplied test asserts that claim is exactly the kind of judgement §2.1 reserves to the agent. The barrier of §6.2.2 does not close it either: §5.5's `target` row keeps `--target` agent-supplied for `gap` ("computed for `mutation`, `--target` for `gap`") and validates it only "as §6.2.3 validates a citation", i.e. the path exists and the line is in range. That is the same flag §5.3.2 struck for mutation on the stated ground that "The evidence chain from experiment to assertion then runs on the patch `cr` executed, not on a flag the agent typed." For a gap probe both the experiment and the pointer back to the finding remain agent-typed, so a test that fails for an unrelated reason plus a `--target` aimed inside the record's own anchor yields a `probed` assertion at severity at least `high`.
suggestion: In §5.4.4 restate the condition as the one `cr` can check — that the record carries a `claim` and the probe's `target` resolves inside the record's anchor — and state plainly that `cr` cannot establish that the supplied test exercises that claim, so a gap probe's `target` is agent-supplied evidence of scope, not of linkage.

finding: Round 10's repair gave the `cited` row a new condition — "and the record's `axis` is not `test`" — which makes `axis` a grading input for the first time. But `axis` is a field the agent writes: §6.1 lists it as "| `axis` | yes | The axis that produced it |" with no `computed` marker, §6.1.4's non-writable list is "`grade`, `state`, `disposition`, `thread_id`, `span_hash`, `issue_hash`, a citation's `content_hash` or `origin`" and does not include it, nothing derives it from the record's `role`, and §1.5's closed-set check binds only "Any `axis` field in a profile, role, or rule" — a record is not on that list. A test-adequacy finding therefore reaches the assertion register by writing `axis: correctness` (or even `axis: testing`, which §6.1.3 accepts because the field is present) and attaching any citation outside its own unit. §4.4.2's "A test-adequacy finding asserts only with an experiment" and the new §6.2 clause both key on a value the producing agent chooses, so the bar they erect is one field-edit deep. §6.2.1's promise that "The grade MUST be computed by `cr` from the record, never asserted by the agent" is contradicted by its own next sentence, which names `axis` as an input.
suggestion: Mark `axis` computed in §6.1: `cr` derives it from the resolved role named by `role` and rejects with exit code 1 a record whose `axis` disagrees, and add `axis` to §6.1.4's list of fields the agent MUST NOT write.

finding: §9.3.6 requires a finding matching the posted index to be "dropped at merge and counted in the round summary", but §10.3's enumeration of what "Every round MUST record there" — "raised, deduplicated, suppressed by thread, waived, forced to question, drafted, posted, discarded as `not-here`, and discarded as `wrong`" — has no key for it. Folding it into `waived` would misreport both counts, since a waiver is a triage decision and a posted-index drop is not. I would have to invent a key name, and §10.3's own justification ("so the history of a review is reconstructable from state alone") fails without one.
suggestion: Add "dropped as already posted per §9.3.6" to §10.3's list of counts.

finding: §4.5.4 names four lenses that must be disclosed with a reason — "a disabled axis, an unavailable axis, the unavailable reinvention half of §4.3.1, and a role skipped per §4.6.4" — and §8.4.3 and §10.1.3 were both harmonised this round to "every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason". §11.1's `--quiet` protection was not, and still names only "The disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4", in a closed list that otherwise pins each protected disclosure individually (the probe cap, the forcing counts, the sandbox recreation notice, the comment cap). With `--quiet` set, implementation A prints all four lenses; implementation B suppresses the unavailable reinvention half and the skipped role as informational messages, since §11.1 is what enumerates the survivors and neither is an axis. I cannot write the `--quiet` honesty test.
suggestion: In §11.1 replace "The disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4" with "Every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason".

finding: Repair 3 made `cited` unreachable on the `test` axis ("and the record's `axis` is not `test`"), but §2.6.1.3 still promises the opposite without condition: "A hit MUST be recorded as a `citations` entry per §6.1 carrying the matched `path`, `line`, and `origin: rule`, which grades the record `cited` per §6.2." §2.6's `axis` field admits any id of §1.5, `test` included, so a detect-carrying rule on the test axis now has two normative answers: §2.6.1.3 says its hit grades the record `cited` (an assertion), §6.2 says `argued` (forced to a question by §6.3).
suggestion: Make the promise conditional: replace "which grades the record `cited` per §6.2" with "which §6.2 may grade `cited`".

finding: The round-10 repair that made `cited` unreachable on the test axis left §2.6.1.3 asserting the opposite. §2.6.1.3 says a mechanical hit "MUST be recorded as a `citations` entry per §6.1 carrying the matched `path`, `line`, and `origin: rule`, which grades the record `cited` per §6.2", stated without qualification. §6.2's `cited` row now reads "...and that entry either has `origin: rule` or lies outside the record's own unit, and the record's `axis` is not `test`", while §2.6's `axis` field is optional with default `convention` and §1.5 admits `test` as a valid value for "any `axis` field in a profile, role, or rule". A `detect` rule declared on the `test` axis therefore produces a hit that §2.6.1.3 grades `cited` and §6.2 grades `argued`. The knock-on is that §8.1.6's provenance trigger — a record that "takes its grade from a citation with `origin: rule`" — never fires for such a record, so the rule id and `rationale` §2.6 item 4 promises the author never reach the posted body.
suggestion: Qualify §2.6.1.3: "...which grades the record `cited` per §6.2 unless the record's `axis` is `test`."

finding: §6.2's `cited` row gained ", and the record's `axis` is not `test`", which falsifies §2.6.1.3's unqualified claim that a detection hit is recorded as a citation "which grades the record `cited` per §6.2". §2.6's schema lets a rule declare any axis of §1.5, `test` included, so a `detect` rule on the `test` axis produces a record that §2.6.1.3 says is `cited` and §6.2 says is `argued`. I would have to choose which of the two sections wins, and the choice decides whether that record is posted as an assertion or forced to a question by §6.3.
suggestion: In §2.6.1.3 replace "which grades the record `cited` per §6.2" with "which grades the record `cited` per §6.2 unless the record's `axis` is `test`".

finding: §2.7 protects exactly three things from the configuration layers: "The confirmation gate of §8.5, the argued forcing of §6.3, and the question label of §8.1.4 are not settings. They MUST NOT be readable from any layer." The two other regions that carry `cr`'s honesty to the author are omitted, and both are justified in the same terms the label is. §8.1.6: "Weak provenance MUST be disclosed in the posted body, not only in the draft the author never sees" — it is the sole channel telling the author that a claim came from a chat note or that an assertion was bought by a regex. §8.1.7 is the sole channel that makes a `probed` or `cited` assertion checkable rather than taken on trust, and it invites a setting by describing itself as "generated by template substitution" with no statement that the template is built in. A `render.*` key or `CR_`-prefixed variable that empties either region would leave the assertions posted and the disclosures gone, which is precisely the failure §2.7 exists to prevent.
suggestion: Extend §2.7's sentence to name the provenance region of §8.1.6 and the evidence region of §8.1.7 alongside the gate, the forcing, and the label.

finding: §4.4.1 requires `cr` to attach to every unit "the test files changed or added by the PR and the symbols they reference". Extracting referenced symbols requires the symbol index of §4.3.1, which exists only when the profile declares `symbols.lang` and `cr` can build one; the `generic` profile that §2.4.5 mandates shipping declares none, so this is a guaranteed case, not a hypothetical. §4.3.1 states its own fallback ("the reinvention half of this axis MUST be marked unavailable per §4.5 rather than skipped silently") but §4.4 states none, so I would have to decide unaided between attaching an empty symbol list and disabling the axis — and the first shrinks the lens with no reason recorded, which §4.5.4 forbids.
suggestion: Append to §4.4.1: "When no symbol index can be built, the symbols MUST be omitted and the omission reported as a lens that did not run per §4.5.4."

finding: §5.1.7's new sentence suppresses a safety rail it meant to keep. It reads "Such a probe establishes nothing in either direction, so §5.3.7 and §5.4.5 MUST NOT be read from it." §5.4.5 is not only the `passed` reading; its second half is a restriction that explicitly covers the result §5.1.7 itself assigns: "It MUST NOT support a `probed` grade, and neither may `timeout`, `error`, `no-tests-selected`, or `inconclusive`; a record resting on one falls to `argued` under §6.2 and is posted as a question. Severity MUST be at most `medium`." §5.1.7 records the unclean probe "with result `error`, overriding the ladder outcome" — squarely inside that clause. Forbidding §5.4.5 from being read therefore lifts the `medium` severity cap for the least trustworthy probe in the spec: a clean gap probe that errors caps its record at `medium`, while one whose sandbox was dirty carries no cap at all. The repair inverts the direction it was written for. (§5.3.7 is a different case: it fires only on result `failed`, which §5.1.7 has already overridden, so excluding it is harmless.)
suggestion: Drop the over-broad half of the citation: "...so §5.3.7 MUST NOT be read from it." §5.4.5 then still applies through its `error` branch, leaving the record `argued` and capped at `medium`.

finding: Repair 6's "Such a probe establishes nothing in either direction, so §5.3.7 and §5.4.5 MUST NOT be read from it" switches off more of §5.4.5 than the ladder outcome. §5.3.7 is purely an establishing clause ("A result of `failed` disproves the gap"), but §5.4.5 carries restrictions as well: "It MUST NOT support a `probed` grade, and neither may `timeout`, `error`, `no-tests-selected`, or `inconclusive`... Severity MUST be at most `medium`." Instructing the reader not to read §5.4.5 from a cleanliness-failed probe removes that severity ceiling — §5.1.7 replaces only the grading half ("MUST NOT grade any finding") and supplies no cap — so a record resting on an errored gap probe may now be raised at `critical` where §5.4.5 held it to `medium`.
suggestion: Name the establishing readings rather than the whole clauses: "so neither §5.3.7's disproof nor §5.4.5's `passed` finding may be read from it".

finding: The two halves of the round-10 baseline repair contradict each other. §5.2.4 says a run record carries `probe` "when the run was performed as part of a probe"; §5.2.6 says "Only a run record carrying no `probe` may serve as a baseline" while requiring `cr probe run` to "perform and record it before the probe" when none exists. The baseline run §5.2.6 mandates is performed as part of a probe run, so under a literal reading it is stamped `probe` and is immediately disqualified from being the baseline it was created to be — no mutation or gap probe can ever be graded at a fresh head. I would have to invent the unstated rule that `probe` is stamped only on the run that executed the mutation or the probe test file.
suggestion: In §5.2.4 replace "`probe` when the run was performed as part of a probe" with "`probe` when the run executed the probe's own mutation or test file; a baseline run performed by `cr probe run` carries none".

finding: §5.2.1 requires recording "the last `tests.output_tail_bytes` of output" and matching `tests.count_pattern` against "the captured output", and §5.5 calls `output_tail` "Runner output truncated" — but no section says which stream that is. Test runners split their summary line between stdout and stderr depending on the runner and on whether a TTY is attached, and capturing them merged makes the interleaving nondeterministic. That decides `tests_run`/`tests_failed`, which decides the §5.3.4 and §5.4.3 rungs and therefore whether a finding can be graded `probed`, and a nondeterministic capture also breaks §2.1.1's reproducibility requirement.
suggestion: Add to §5.2.1: "Output means the runner's stdout and stderr captured separately and concatenated in that order; both `output_tail` and `tests.count_pattern` apply to that concatenation."

finding: Repair 1 keys the new field on the wrong event. §5.2.4 now stores `probe` "when the run was performed as part of a probe", and §5.2.6 adds "Only a run record carrying no `probe` may serve as a baseline." But §5.2.6's own first sentence makes `cr probe run` perform the baseline: "when no matching run exists at the current head, MUST perform and record it before the probe." That baseline run is literally performed as part of a probe invocation, so under §5.2.4's trigger it is stamped `probe` and the very next sentence disqualifies it — a first probe at a fresh head can never obtain a usable baseline. Only §5.5's gloss ("unmutated, un-probed code") hints at the intended narrower trigger, and it is not the clause an implementer of §5.2.4 reads.
suggestion: Key the field on what the run measured, not on which command ran it: in §5.2.4 replace "`probe` when the run was performed as part of a probe" with "`probe` when the run measured that probe's mutated or injected code".

finding: The repaired §5.3.2 derivation yields only a line number, but §5.5 requires `target` to be `path:line` and §6.2.2 compares that path against the record's anchor path. Nothing says which patch header supplies the path or how an `a/`/`b/` prefix is stripped to the repo-relative form anchors use, and nothing constrains the patch to one file or one hunk — §5.3.1's "a unified diff against a sandbox file" is descriptive, not a validated MUST. For a two-hunk patch whose first hunk only adds lines and whose second removes one, "the pre-image line number of the first line the patch removes or replaces" and "for a hunk that only adds lines, the pre-image line the additions follow" both match and give different answers; for a two-file patch there is no defined path at all.
suggestion: Add to §5.3.2: "The patch MUST touch exactly one file and MUST otherwise be rejected with exit code 1. `target`'s path is that file's post-image path relative to the repository root, and its line is derived from the patch's first hunk."

finding: §5.3.2 applies an agent-supplied unified diff inside the sandbox with no requirement that the paths it names stay inside the sandbox. §5.1.4 states the guarantee — "`cr` MUST NOT modify the user's main worktree, index, or current branch" — but names no enforcement, and the cleanliness checks of §5.1.6 and §5.1.7 only inspect the sandbox, so a patch carrying `../` components or aimed at a symlink pointing out of the worktree would breach the guarantee undetected and unreverted. Whether the invariant holds would depend entirely on which patch-application mechanism I happened to pick.
suggestion: Add to §5.3.2: "A patch naming a path that resolves outside the sandbox root, or that traverses a symlink, MUST be rejected with exit code 1 before anything is applied."

finding: §5.3.2's derivation is not a function of an arbitrary unified diff: "the pre-image line number of the first line the patch removes or replaces, or for a hunk that only adds lines, the pre-image line the additions follow, or the hunk's first pre-image line when it inserts at the top". Branch 1 is scoped to the whole patch ("the patch removes"); branches 2 and 3 are scoped to a hunk ("a hunk that only adds lines"), and nothing says which hunk or that a patch has only one. For a two-hunk patch whose first hunk only adds lines and whose second deletes one, implementation A applies the branches in order and targets the deleted line in hunk 2; implementation B evaluates the branches per hunk starting at hunk 1 and targets hunk 1's insertion point. The same split occurs for a patch touching two files, where the two candidate targets carry different `path`s. Because §6.2.2 grades on whether `target` "falls within that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range on the same path", the two implementations disagree on whether the record is graded `probed` or rejected with exit code 1.
suggestion: Bind the derivation to a single hunk: require a mutation patch to contain exactly one hunk in one file, rejecting any other with exit code 1, and derive `target` from that hunk.

finding: §6.2.1's enumeration of grading inputs is closed and contradicted two sentences later by its own containment rule. It states "The only inputs are `axis`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record", then defines "a `path:line` is **inside** a unit when `path` is one of that unit's file paths and `line` falls within the head-side range of one of its hunks". §6.2's `cited` row needs that predicate, which reads the record's `unit` and the unit's hunks; §6.2.2 admits `probed` only when the probe's "`target` falls within that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range on the same path", which reads `anchor`. Neither `unit` nor `anchor` appears in the closed set, so an implementation honouring the sentence as written cannot compute either grade. The closing claim "no field the agent writes can move a location across the boundary" is also false as stated, since `unit` and `anchor` are both agent-supplied per §6.1.
suggestion: Extend the enumeration to the fields grading actually reads: "The only inputs are `axis`, `unit`, `anchor`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record".

finding: §6.2.1's enumeration, extended in this round, is now demonstrably incomplete: "The only inputs are `axis`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record". Grading also reads two further record fields. `probed` requires per §6.2.2 that the probe's `target` "falls within that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range on the same path", and `cited` requires a citation that "lies outside the record's own unit", which reads `unit`. This is observable at triage: §7.2's marker table makes `path`, `start_line`, and `line` editable, and §7.2.2 requires that "`cr post` MUST recompute every record's grade". Implementation A recomputes containment and drops a record from `probed` to `argued` — hence to a posted question — after the reviewer narrows the anchor past the probe target; implementation B holds §6.2.1's closed list and keeps it `probed`. I cannot write the post-edit grade assertion either way.
suggestion: Extend the list in §6.2.1 to "`axis`, `unit`, `anchor`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record".

finding: §6.2.1's repaired sentence reads "The only inputs are `axis`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record", but grading cannot be computed from those three. The same item evaluates containment against "the record's own unit" (which needs the record's `unit` field plus that unit's hunk ranges from `units.ndjson`), and §6.2.2 supports `probed` only when the probe's `target` "falls within that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range on the same path" (which needs the record's `anchor`). Taken literally the enumeration is insufficient, and I would have to decide on my own which further record fields the grader is permitted to read — the exact question the sentence exists to close.
suggestion: In §6.2.1 replace "The only inputs are `axis`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record" with "The only inputs are `axis`, `unit`, `anchor`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record".

finding: §5.4.4 records a limit `cr` knows and the author never learns: "A `failed` gap probe means either the behaviour is wrong or the supplied test is wrong, and `cr` cannot distinguish the two." Such a probe nevertheless supports a `probed` grade at severity at least `high`, and §8.1.7's evidence region carries only "the probe's `kind`, `target`, `filter`, `result`, and `output_tail`" — a reader sees `kind: gap, result: failed` under a comment written in the assertion register and has no way to know the result is ambiguous between two causes, one of which is the reviewer's own test. The spec already does this correctly one section earlier: §5.3.6 requires a filtered mutation probe's narrower guarantee to be "carried into the §8.1.7 evidence region" and forbids stating it "more widely than the empty selection it actually catches". The parallel obligation for the gap probe's two-cause ambiguity is missing, so `cr` claims more than it established, in the one register where the author has no label warning them to discount it.
suggestion: Add to §8.1.7 that for a `gap` probe with result `failed` the evidence region MUST state that the test was supplied by the reviewer and that the result does not distinguish a wrong behaviour from a wrong test, per §5.4.4.

finding: Repair 5 widened the §4.5.4 gloss at both of its downstream call sites — §8.4.3 now reads "the active axes, and every lens that did not run, with its reason" and §10.1.3 "Active axes, and every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run, with its reason" — but left the third occurrence narrow. §11.1's always-print list still enumerates only "The disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4", so the two lenses repair 5 was written to surface (a role skipped per §4.6.4 and the unavailable reinvention half of §4.3.1) are absent from the enumeration that `--quiet` may not suppress.
suggestion: In §11.1 replace "The disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4" with "The lenses of §4.5.4 that did not run".

finding: §3.6.1 and §3.6.2 both carry `--source <source>` in their signatures and §3.6.3 closes the vocabulary to five values, but nothing says whether the flag is required or what source a note carries when it is omitted — while §3.6.1 requires every note to be appended "with an id ..., a timestamp, the PR it came from, and the source", so the field is never absent. §11's command table lists both `cr note` and `cr answer` without the flag at all. I would have to invent either a hard requirement or a default, and §8.1.6 discloses a note's source to the author, so the invented value reaches a human.
suggestion: Add to §3.6.3: "`--source` is required on `cr note` and `cr answer`; a missing or out-of-vocabulary value MUST abort with exit code 2."

finding: §4.4.2 states the grading rule as "Citations to test files MUST NOT grade it `cited`", a per-citation predicate, while §6.2's repaired `cited` row states it as a per-record one — no record whose `axis` is `test` can be `cited`, whatever its citations point at. Implementing §4.4.2 as written needs an "is a test file" predicate the grader never computes and the spec never defines for grading (only `tests.globs`, "Patterns identifying test files", exists, for selecting probe paths and test runs). §6.2.1 also says grading's inputs are fixed, so §4.4.2 asserts a rule the authoritative grader cannot implement.
suggestion: Replace §4.4.2's first clause with "A `test`-axis record can never be graded `cited` per §6.2, so without a supporting probe it is `argued` and is posted as a question per §6.3."

finding: §5.1.7 voids a probe whose post-run cleanliness check fails — "MUST be recorded with result `error`, overriding the ladder outcome, MUST NOT grade any finding... Such a probe establishes nothing in either direction" — but nothing does the same for a run record, and §5.1.7's "The post-run cleanliness check" is introduced with a definite article for something §5.1.6 defines only as a pre-run check. §5.2.5 derives `passed` from `exit_code`, `tests_run`, and `tests_failed` alone, and §5.2.6's only added restriction is that the record carry no `probe`. For a suite that writes a tracked file while running, one tester asserts the resulting baseline is unusable, by analogy with §5.1.7; another asserts it is `passed: true` and may grade a later mutation probe `probed`. §5.1.6's pre-run check recreates the sandbox before the next run but never touches the run record already written.
suggestion: Add one clause to §5.1.7: "A test run whose post-run check fails MUST be recorded with `passed: false`."

finding: Round 10's baseline guard turns on a phrase that reads against itself. §5.2.4 stamps a run record with "`probe` when the run was performed as part of a probe", and §5.2.6 closes with "Only a run record carrying no `probe` may serve as a baseline" — but the sentence immediately before it requires `cr probe run` to "perform and record" the baseline itself when none exists at the current head. That baseline run is literally performed as part of a probe invocation, so a straightforward reading stamps it and then disqualifies it, leaving `cr probe run` unable to produce a usable baseline and no probe able to reach `probed`. The intended meaning is the run of mutated or probe-injected code, and the barrier that carries an assertion should not depend on the reader reconstructing it by contradiction.
suggestion: In §5.2.4 replace "when the run was performed as part of a probe" with "when the run measured mutated or probe-injected code", so the baseline `cr` records under §5.2.6 is unambiguously eligible.

finding: Repair 8 retired the ambiguous `§2.6.<n>` form in §2.4's `rules` row and §2.6.1.3 in favour of "§2.6 item 1" and "§2.6 item 3", because §2.6 is the one section carrying both a numbered list and subsections. One occurrence was missed: §8.1.6 still cites "the rule id with its `rationale` per §2.6.4", which addresses §2.6's numbered item 4 in exactly the form repair 8 declared ambiguous. It resolves only because no `#### 2.6.4` heading happens to exist.
suggestion: Replace "per §2.6.4" with "per §2.6 item 4".

finding: §8.4.3 makes `cr` compose reader-facing prose in the review body — "the disclosure of §4.5.4 — the active axes, and every lens that did not run, with its reason" — but no rule fixes its language. §8.1.1 scopes `render.lang` to "Comment bodies", and §8.4.3 exempts the review body only from §1.6.1. Every other `cr`-owned string the author reads has a rule (§8.1.4's label "MUST be built in per `render.lang`"); this one does not, so I would have to pick English or `render.lang` and the honesty disclosure could reach the author in a language they do not read.
suggestion: Add to §8.4.3: "The disclosure MUST be built in per `render.lang`, as §8.1.4's label is."
